attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's ruling that R7.3 was HALF right. A universal law does need a domain — that half stands, and the LPM prior art backs it. But R7.3 then IDENTIFIED the ten conceptual channel rows with the universe, and they are not it: the tenth row reads `anything else permitted to influence the transition`, which is not a controlled object type but a catch-all standing in for the fact that the universe is not known. In LPM the universe is not a prose list of provenance meanings — it is the set of controlled data types the kernel actually mediates, and the completeness result is that a hook lies on ALL CONTROL PATHS to operations on them. The universe ARISES FROM the mediation surface; it is not authored beside it. So: MediationUniverse = UNBUILT, would be derived from the input/effect capabilities a World/TRVM boundary exposes to an isolated inference operation; ChannelCatalog = DECLARED, the semantic taxonomy that will classify members of U once U exists; ASM-MEDIATION-UNIVERSE = UNDISCHARGED. That triple is the strongest honest state and R7.3 was one word away from it.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6, ruling on ROUND7_3_MOSAIC_BRIEF.md §8.1. SRC-BATES-2015-LPM for how a universe is actually obtained.

attrs.review_focus: DECLARED, not proved: this records where the universe must come from and that it is absent. The risk it creates is that `UNBUILT` reads as a promise. Nothing here is building a World/TRVM boundary and nothing in this lane is scheduled to.
attrs.statement: The mediation universe, the channel catalog, and the assumption binding them are three separate objects, and only the catalog exists.
